description:
What the OWOX Data Marts Facebook Ads connector loads from Meta, and how the pieces fit
together. Every table belongs to one ad account. Under it, ads sit in ad sets and campaigns
and each ad runs one creative from the account's library; the performance tables report
each ad day by day, either whole or split by audience, place, device, product or link.

The account is the anchor. The entity tables [Ads](./ads.md) and
[Ad Creatives](./ad-creatives.md) and the three unsplit performance tables
([Ad Insights](./ad-insights.md), [Ad Insights by Ad Set](./ad-insights-by-ad-set.md) and
[Ad Insights by Campaign](./ad-insights-by-campaign.md)) carry `account_id`, the bare
account number, and join to [Ad Account](./ad-account.md) on it. The breakdown tables reach
the account through Ad Insights, [Ad](./ad.md) through Ads, and
[Ad Account User](./ad-account-user.md) joins it on `id`, the `act_` form it carries.
Performance reaches an ad's name, status and creative through [Ads](./ads.md) on `ad_id`.
Campaigns and ad sets have no table of their own in this connector — their IDs and names
travel on every performance row, and their deduplicated reach comes from the two
level-specific tables.

Two cautions matter more than any single field. **Reach and frequency do not add up**:
summing them across ads, days or breakdown values counts the same person several times;
take them from [Ad Insights by Ad Set](./ad-insights-by-ad-set.md) or
[Ad Insights by Campaign](./ad-insights-by-campaign.md). And **the ad tables are snapshots of what
exists now**: Meta omits deleted and archived ads, so older performance rows can point at
an ad that is no longer listed.
questions: Which campaigns spend the most for the fewest results, once spend is divided by results?
Which creatives drive the cheapest conversions, once performance is joined to the creative each ad runs?
How many people did each campaign reach on a given day, and how often did they see the ads?

Ad Account.description:
The ad account itself: its name, currency, time zone, status, spend cap and the business that owns it. Every other table in this connector belongs to exactly one account. [Ads](./ads.md), [Ad Creatives](./ad-creatives.md) and the three unsplit performance tables ([Ad Insights](./ad-insights.md), [Ad Insights by Ad Set](./ad-insights-by-ad-set.md) and [Ad Insights by Campaign](./ad-insights-by-campaign.md)) join here on `account_id`; the breakdown tables reach it through Ad Insights, [Ad](./ad.md) through Ads, and [Ad Account User](./ad-account-user.md) joins on `id`. Note the two identifiers: `id` is `act_` followed by the number, the form Ad Account User also carries, while `account_id` is the bare number that the ads, creatives and insights tables carry.

The currency and time zone here are what every amount and every date in the account's reports are expressed in, so accounts in different currencies cannot be summed without conversion.
questions: Which accounts are close to their spend cap?
What currency and time zone does each account use?
Which business does each account belong to, and what is its status?

alternateKeys.source: https://developers.facebook.com/docs/marketing-api/reference/ad-account/ (account_id: "The ID of the Ad Account."; id: "The string `act_{ad_account_id}`.") Each alone identifies the account; the connector lists both as its unique key.

Ad Account User.description: Named in the connector for the users assigned to an ad account. As the connector currently requests it, it returns the account's own `id` (`act_` plus the number) and `name`, one row per account.
questions: Which accounts does the connector read, by id and name?
How many accounts are loaded?
Do the names here match the names in Ad Account?

Ad Creatives.description:
The creatives in the account's library: body text, title, image and video, call to action, destination link, URL tags and the Page post the ad is built on. A creative is reusable — several ads can run the same one — and it cannot be edited in place: changing an ad's content means creating a new creative and pointing the ad at it, so an ad's creative can change during its life.

`effective_object_story_id` is the Page post the ad actually uses, as `<page_id>_<post_id>`; prefer it to `object_story_id`, which is empty when the post was created together with the ad.
questions: Which call to action types are used by the most creatives?
Which creatives share the same Page post (`effective_object_story_id`)?
Which creatives are not in an active status?

Ads.description:
One row per ad, with its name, status, the campaign and ad set it sits in, the creative it currently runs, and when it was created and last updated. It is the only table that names an ad's creative, so it is the bridge from performance to creative content.

It is a snapshot of the ads that exist now. Meta leaves deleted and archived ads out of this list by default, so performance rows for an ad removed since will find no match here — join from insights with that in mind. `effective_status` is what Meta is actually doing with the ad (it inherits a paused campaign or ad set), while `status` is only what was set on the ad itself.
questions: How many ads are active, paused or with issues in each campaign?
Which ads run the same creative?
Which ads were updated in the last 30 days?

Ad.description: The older view of the same ads (Meta's API still calls an ad an "ad group"). It carries the same ads as [Ads](./ads.md), since the connector reads both from the account's ads list, and adds a few fields — review feedback, schedule, bid amount, tracking specs and flattened creative fields. Prefer [Ads](./ads.md) unless you need one of those. Like [Ads](./ads.md), it lists only ads that still exist.
questions: Which ads were copied from another ad (`source_ad_id` is set)?
Which ads have review feedback or delivery issues?
Which ads have an end time scheduled?

Ad Insights.description:
The base performance table: no breakdown, so each ad-day appears once. Start here for spend, clicks, conversions and ROAS by campaign, ad set or ad.

One row per ad per day, as Meta reports it. Spend, impressions and clicks add up across ads and days; **reach, frequency and every `unique_*` metric do not** — they count people, and a person who saw two ads is one person, so summing them overstates the audience. Take reach from [Ad Insights by Ad Set](./ad-insights-by-ad-set.md) or [Ad Insights by Campaign](./ad-insights-by-campaign.md), where Meta deduplicates it. Conversions follow the attribution window of the request; since January 2026 Meta no longer returns the 7-day and 28-day view windows, so older history pulled with them will not match a fresh pull.
questions: What did each ad spend and return per day over the last 30 days?
Which campaigns have the highest cost per click, once their ads are rolled up through `campaign_id`?
Which ads reach the fewest people while spending the most?

Ad Insights by Age and Gender.description:
The same ad-day, split by the age band and gender Meta attributes to the people reached. People Meta cannot classify land in `unknown`, which is a real share of delivery rather than an error.

One row per ad, per day, per age band and gender, as Meta reports it. Spend, impressions and clicks add up across ads, days and breakdown values; **reach, frequency and every `unique_*` metric do not** — they count people, and a person who saw two ads is one person, so summing them overstates the audience. Take reach from [Ad Insights by Ad Set](./ad-insights-by-ad-set.md) or [Ad Insights by Campaign](./ad-insights-by-campaign.md), where Meta deduplicates it. Conversions follow the attribution window of the request; since January 2026 Meta no longer returns the 7-day and 28-day view windows, so older history pulled with them will not match a fresh pull.
questions: Which age and gender groups give the cheapest clicks?
How do impressions split by gender within each age range?
Which age ranges convert best for a given ad (`actions`, `spend`)?

Ad Insights by Country.description:
The same ad-day, split by the country the people reached are in.

One row per ad, per day, per country, as Meta reports it. Spend, impressions and clicks add up across ads, days and breakdown values; **reach, frequency and every `unique_*` metric do not** — they count people, and a person who saw two ads is one person, so summing them overstates the audience. Take reach from [Ad Insights by Ad Set](./ad-insights-by-ad-set.md) or [Ad Insights by Campaign](./ad-insights-by-campaign.md), where Meta deduplicates it. Conversions follow the attribution window of the request; since January 2026 Meta no longer returns the 7-day and 28-day view windows, so older history pulled with them will not match a fresh pull.
questions: Which countries get the most spend, and what do they return?
Which ads spend in the most countries?
How does the click-through rate differ between countries?

Ad Insights by Region.description:
The same ad-day, split by region within a country — a state, province or similar division. Some video metrics are not available with this breakdown.

One row per ad, per day, per region, as Meta reports it. Spend, impressions and clicks add up across ads, days and breakdown values; **reach, frequency and every `unique_*` metric do not** — they count people, and a person who saw two ads is one person, so summing them overstates the audience. Take reach from [Ad Insights by Ad Set](./ad-insights-by-ad-set.md) or [Ad Insights by Campaign](./ad-insights-by-campaign.md), where Meta deduplicates it. Conversions follow the attribution window of the request; since January 2026 Meta no longer returns the 7-day and 28-day view windows, so older history pulled with them will not match a fresh pull.
questions: Which regions bring the most clicks per unit of spend?
Which regions get impressions but few clicks?
How does spend split across regions for each campaign?

Ad Insights by Device Platform.description:
The same ad-day, split by the device the ad was shown on — mobile or desktop.

One row per ad, per day, per device platform, as Meta reports it. Spend, impressions and clicks add up across ads, days and breakdown values; **reach, frequency and every `unique_*` metric do not** — they count people, and a person who saw two ads is one person, so summing them overstates the audience. Take reach from [Ad Insights by Ad Set](./ad-insights-by-ad-set.md) or [Ad Insights by Campaign](./ad-insights-by-campaign.md), where Meta deduplicates it. Conversions follow the attribution window of the request; since January 2026 Meta no longer returns the 7-day and 28-day view windows, so older history pulled with them will not match a fresh pull.
questions: Do mobile and desktop differ in click-through rate?
How does spend split across device platforms for each campaign?
Which ads depend most on one device platform?

Ad Insights by Publisher Platform and Po.description:
The same ad-day, split by where the ad appeared: the platform (Facebook, Instagram, Messenger, Audience Network, Threads) and the placement inside it (Feed, Stories, Reels, in-stream video and so on).

One row per ad, per day, per platform and placement, as Meta reports it. Spend, impressions and clicks add up across ads, days and breakdown values; **reach, frequency and every `unique_*` metric do not** — they count people, and a person who saw two ads is one person, so summing them overstates the audience. Take reach from [Ad Insights by Ad Set](./ad-insights-by-ad-set.md) or [Ad Insights by Campaign](./ad-insights-by-campaign.md), where Meta deduplicates it. Conversions follow the attribution window of the request; since January 2026 Meta no longer returns the 7-day and 28-day view windows, so older history pulled with them will not match a fresh pull.
questions: Which placements cost the least per click?
How does spend split across platforms and positions for each campaign?
Which positions get the most impressions without clicks?

Ad Insights by Product ID.description:
The same ad-day, split by catalog product. It is filled only for catalog ads — Advantage+ catalog and other dynamic product formats; other ads have no product to report.

One row per ad, per day, per catalog product, as Meta reports it. Spend, impressions and clicks add up across ads, days and breakdown values; **reach, frequency and every `unique_*` metric do not** — they count people, and a person who saw two ads is one person, so summing them overstates the audience. Take reach from [Ad Insights by Ad Set](./ad-insights-by-ad-set.md) or [Ad Insights by Campaign](./ad-insights-by-campaign.md), where Meta deduplicates it. Conversions follow the attribution window of the request; since January 2026 Meta no longer returns the 7-day and 28-day view windows, so older history pulled with them will not match a fresh pull.
questions: Which products get the most spend?
Which products have the most clicks per impression?
Which products appear in the most ads?

Ad Insights by Link URL Asset.description:
The same ad-day, split by the destination URL asset the ad used. It is filled only for ads that carry several links — dynamic creative and multi-link formats; a single-link ad has nothing to split. With short-link processing on, the resolved landing page sits in `link_url_asset.parsed_url`.

One row per ad, per day, per link URL asset, as Meta reports it. Spend, impressions and clicks add up across ads, days and breakdown values; **reach, frequency and every `unique_*` metric do not** — they count people, and a person who saw two ads is one person, so summing them overstates the audience. Take reach from [Ad Insights by Ad Set](./ad-insights-by-ad-set.md) or [Ad Insights by Campaign](./ad-insights-by-campaign.md), where Meta deduplicates it. Conversions follow the attribution window of the request; since January 2026 Meta no longer returns the 7-day and 28-day view windows, so older history pulled with them will not match a fresh pull.
questions: Which link URLs get the most clicks?
Which ads send traffic to more than one URL?
Which link URLs cost the most per click?

Ad Insights by Ad Set.description: Daily performance at the ad-set level, requested from Meta at that level so that reach and frequency are deduplicated across the ad set's ads — these numbers match Meta Ads Manager. Use it for audience size and frequency; use [Ad Insights](./ad-insights.md) when you need the ad behind a number. The two should not be joined row to row: they describe the same delivery at two levels, so combining them counts it twice.
questions: How many people did each ad set reach on a given day, and how often did they see it?
Which optimization goals have the lowest cost per click?
Which ad sets spend the most within each campaign?

Ad Insights by Campaign.description: Daily performance at the campaign level, requested from Meta at that level so that reach and frequency are deduplicated across the campaign's ad sets and ads — these numbers match Meta Ads Manager. It is the right source for campaign reach, frequency and budget pacing; it should not be joined row to row with the ad-level tables, which describe the same delivery in more detail.
questions: How many people did each campaign reach on a given day, and how often did they see it?
Which campaigns have the highest spend for the lowest click-through rate?
How does spend per day change within each objective?
